title: Buddhist Suttas
altTitles: Sacred Books of the East, vol. 11
subcategory: Dīgha Nikāya and Majjhima Nikāya selections
attributionNote: The discourses are presented in the canon as the Buddha's teaching, transmitted by the early Buddhist community. The Pali text is anonymous and collective.
description: This volume collects seven discourses that stand at the centre of Theravada scripture: the Book of the Great Decease, the Buddha's last journey and final instructions; the Foundation of the Kingdom of Righteousness, his first sermon; the Tevigga on knowledge of the Vedas; the Akankheyya on desire; the Ketokhila on barrenness and bondage; the Mahā-Sudassana legend of the great king of glory; and the Sabbāsava on the destruction of the intoxicants.
historicalContext: T. W. Rhys Davids translated these suttas for the Sacred Books of the East, volume 11 (1881). The Mahāparinibbāna-Suttanta in particular remains a standard English rendering and shaped the modern understanding of the Buddha's final days.
availabilityNote: Complete for this volume. All seven suttas are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one sutta per chapter. The volume's general introduction is not part of the work.
